sentences.text: THE HONOURABLE SRI JUSTICE K.SURENDER  CRIMINAL APPEAL No.1318 OF 2011 JUDGMENT:

1. The State aggrieved by the acquittal of the respondents preferred the present appeal questioning the judgment dated 14.11.2003.
2.
Briefly, the case of the prosecution is that on 30.12.1999, P.W.1 inspected the premises of A-1 and found 49 kgs. of 'moongdal' in a loose gunny bag kept for sale to public for human consumption.
Having served notice in accordance with the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, samples were drawn and sent for analysis on 31.12.1999.
Having obtained the public analyst report, on the basis of the report of the Director, complaint was filed by P.W.1/Food Inspector.

During the course of trial, learned Magistrate examined P.Ws.1 and 2 and marked Ex.P.1 to P.45.
3.

The main ground on which the acquittal was recorded is that the accused had lost opportunity of sending the second sample drawn during the search to Central Food Laboratory (C.F.L.) in view of the delay in lodging the complaint.
According to the learned Magistrate, there was a delay of more than two years in filing the complaint.
Since the accused have lost their opportunity, the learned Magistrate found that the accused are entitled for acquittal.
It was further found that the names of A-4 to A-6 were not mentioned in the written consent order of the Director for launching prosecution.
4. Learned Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of the State would submit that there are valid grounds to interfere with the orders of acquittal.
Though notices were ordered, they are not served till date.
The case is of the year 1999, Calendar Case is of the year 2002 and the judgment was passed in the year, 2003.

5. Though lapse of time may not be a ground to dismiss the appeal filed by the State, however, in the present facts and circumstances of the case, when the valuable opportunity/right of the accused to send second sample to C.F.L was not available on account of delay in filing the complaint, I do not find any reason to interfere with the well reasoned judgment of the trial Court.
6. The Criminal Appeal fails and accordingly, it is dismissed.
Miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
K.SURENDER, J Date: 05.06.2023 dv The Food Inspector, Rep.By P.P., ... vs G. Ramesh, Hyderabad, And 7 Otrs.
